meta.subtitle: Replacement kit: 22 of 24x Samsung 64 GB DDR5-5600 active (1.385 TB) - Tyrone MDA200A2N-224
meta.platform: Tyrone MDA200A2N-224 / 2x AMD EPYC 9135 (32C/64T, Zen 5 Turin)

executive_summary: Post-install revalidation of a replacement DIMM kit in server 172.16.11.132 (Tyrone MDA200A2N-224, dual AMD EPYC 9135). The kit is a complete physical swap - zero serial overlap with this morning's 24-module set. Result: only 22 of 24 modules train. BIOS maps out the modules in P0 CHANNEL C and P1 CHANNEL L on every boot: ACPI BERT carries fatal 'Storage error in DRAM memory - physical memory map-out event' records for locators P0MC0 and P1ML0, and the BMC SEL asserts 'Memory Device Disabled' (CPU0 + CPU1) on all three post-swap boots. Usable capacity is 1.385 TB instead of 1.5 TB.

The 22 active modules are electrically healthy: the 5-minute 100% burn held 1272 GB (92% of RAM) resident across 64 verify-mode workers (1.47 billion operations) with zero errors, zero OOM/swap, EDAC CE=0/UE=0, zero machine-checks and zero new SEL entries during the campaign; cores held full boost (peak 4342 MHz vs 4300 rated).

However, the asymmetric 11+11-channel population cripples aggregate bandwidth: 348.6 GB/s vs 581.1 GB/s on the 24-DIMM baseline measured this morning (-40%); DRAM-bound sysbench read/write drop 42%/56%. Single-thread memcpy (22.8 GB/s) and the NUMA-remote ratio (1.62x) are unaffected, isolating the regression to interleave geometry, not module speed or fabric health. Verdict: FAIL as installed - reseat/replace the two mapped-out modules and re-screen before deployment.

comparison.caption: Same server, same day, same tooling - only the DIMM kit changed (complete swap, zero serial overlap).
comparison.notes: Losing one channel per socket leaves an asymmetric 11+11-channel population: the EPYC UMC interleave falls back to a degraded geometry costing ~40% aggregate bandwidth (348.6 vs 581.1 GB/s) and 42-56% on DRAM-bound sysbench, while single-thread memcpy (-4%) and the NUMA-remote ratio (1.62x vs 1.60x) stay normal - proof the regression is interleave geometry, not module speed, thermal or fabric health. Usable capacity drops 1.5 TB -> 1.385 TB.

sel_status: BMC SEL: 0 new entries during the campaign (323 before and after). The 44 entries added between Run 1 and Run 2 (279 -> 323) document the swap session: PSU AC-loss/presence and chassis-intrusion artifacts at 08:33/08:48/08:57 (benign - AC pulled during physical work), three boots, and 'Memory Device Disabled' asserted for CPU0 + CPU1 on every boot (08:45:13, 08:53:10, 09:02:54).
dmesg_status: ACPI BERT (firmware-first) carries two FATAL memory error records from POST: 'Storage error in DRAM memory (0x40400) ... error_type 15, physical memory map-out event' at locator P0MC0 (node 0, card 0) and locator P1ML0 (node 1, card 8) - firmware mapped both modules out before OS handoff. During the campaign itself: 0 machine-check events, AMD EDAC CE=0/UE=0 on both controllers, core clocks 4107-4342 MHz under load, swap untouched, no OOM-killer activity.
findings: Two of the 24 replacement modules fail DRAM training and are mapped out by firmware on every boot. Evidence chain: dmidecode shows no SPD data for P0 CHANNEL C and P1 CHANNEL L; BMC SEL asserts 'Memory Device Disabled' (CPU0 + CPU1) on all three post-swap boots; ACPI BERT records fatal 'Storage error in DRAM memory - physical memory map-out event' at locators P0MC0 and P1ML0. Usable memory drops to 1.385 TB (22x 64 GB), one channel lost per socket.

Aggregate bandwidth collapses 40% as installed: 348.6 GB/s vs the 581.1 GB/s 24-DIMM baseline measured this morning with identical tooling. DRAM-bound sysbench drops 42% (read, 206.8 GB/s) and 56% (write, 90.8 GB/s). The asymmetric 11+11-channel population forces the EPYC UMC interleave into a degraded geometry - the penalty far exceeds the 8% capacity loss.

The regression is isolated to interleave geometry: single-thread memcpy is unchanged (22.8 vs 23.8 GB/s), the NUMA-remote ratio is unchanged (1.62x vs 1.60x), all 22 active modules train at full 5600 MT/s, and cores held 4107-4342 MHz under load - ruling out module speed, fabric, thermal and clock causes.

The 22 active modules are electrically healthy: 5-minute 100% burn at 1272 GB resident (92% of usable RAM), stress-ng full pattern sweep with --verify completed 1,473,163,606 operations - zero verification failures, zero OOM, swap untouched; EDAC CE=0/UE=0; zero machine-checks; zero new SEL entries during the campaign.

Kit identity recorded for traceability: complete physical swap - zero serial overlap with the Run-1 set. 17 modules from lot family 80CE04254642E0xxxx, 5 from newer lot 80CE04254742EE/EFxxxx; all Samsung M321R8GA0PB0-CWMCJ, 2R, 80-bit (64+16 ECC). Full slot-by-slot map incl. the two disabled positions in the Hardware Inventory section. The mapped-out modules' serials are not electronically readable - record them from the label during reseat.

The PSU 'Failure detected' and chassis-intrusion SEL entries between 08:33 and 08:57 are maintenance artifacts (AC pulled while the chassis was open for the swap); both supplies re-asserted presence on every power-up and the post-test package power (187 W idle) is normal.
recommendations: Reseat the modules in P0 CHANNEL C and P1 CHANNEL L and re-run this 20-minute screen. If either position still maps out, swap that module with a known-good neighbour to isolate module vs slot: fault follows module -> RMA the module (BERT 'storage error in DRAM' is a module-internal failure signature); fault stays with slot -> board-level action.

Do NOT deploy this configuration for bandwidth-sensitive workloads: -40% aggregate bandwidth as installed. Restoring 12+12 symmetric channels should return ~581 GB/s (today's 24-DIMM baseline on this exact box).
Record the two failed modules' label serials during the reseat (SPD is not electronically readable while mapped out) and keep both per-module serial maps (Run 1 + Run 2 reports) for RMA paperwork.
If a module must be permanently removed, prefer a SYMMETRIC reduced population per AMD population rules over an asymmetric 11+11 layout - asymmetry is what destroys interleaving.
Install rasdaemon and enable BIOS patrol scrub before production so any future in-service DIMM degradation is logged per-DIMM between validation campaigns.
